title: A Strange Moment for the U.S. Economy

sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 你不会想错过的。

sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Why is the economic recovery from the pandemic so uneven?
sentences.zh: 为什么大流行之后的经济复苏如此不均衡？

sentences.en: Why are companies finding it so hard to hire?
sentences.zh: 为什么公司发现招聘如此困难？

sentences.en: Why are the prices of used cars surging?
sentences.zh: 为什么二手车价格飙升？

sentences.en: Kevin Roos talked to our colleague, business reporter Ben Castleman, about this strange moment in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 凯文·鲁斯与我们的同事、商业记者本·卡斯特尔曼谈论了美国当前这个奇怪的时刻

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 经济。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, May 18th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月18日，星期二。

sentences.en: Ben, hello.
sentences.zh: 本，你好。

sentences.en: Kevin.
sentences.zh: 凯文。

sentences.en: You look great.
sentences.zh: 你看起来真棒。

sentences.en: Your hair is luxurious and pandemic-grown, and it's, you know, you're radiant.
sentences.zh: 你的头发很丰盈，带着疫情期间生长的痕迹，而且，你知道的，你容光焕发。

sentences.en: I'm finally almost ready to get a haircut, to sheer off the COVID locks.
sentences.zh: 我终于差不多准备好理发了，把疫情期间长出的头发剪掉。

sentences.en: Ben, you are my personal, I was going to say economics guru, but it's more like economics
sentences.zh: 本，你是我私人的，我本来想说是经济学大师，但更像是经济学

sentences.en: therapist because I come to you when I'm very worried about something and you explain patiently why I shouldn't be that worried about it.
sentences.zh: 治疗师，因为当我为某事非常担心时我就会来找你，而你耐心地向我解释为什么我不必为此那么担心。

sentences.en: And so, lately, most of my questions have been essentially some version of like, am I crazy here?
sentences.zh: 所以，最近我的大部分问题基本上都是某种版本的：我是不是疯了？

sentences.en: Like, what is happening in the economy right now?
sentences.zh: 比如，现在经济到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: You know, tons of people are obviously still struggling from the pandemic, but, you know, housing prices are going insane all over the country.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，显然有成千上万的人仍在饱受疫情困扰，但是，你知道的，全国各地的房价都在疯狂上涨。

sentences.en: People are getting rich on Dogecoin and other weird investments.
sentences.zh: 人们通过狗狗币和其他奇怪的投资发家致富。

sentences.en: Millions of people are still out of jobs, but there's also these weird labor shortages where businesses can't find enough people to work.
sentences.zh: 数百万人仍然失业，但同时也存在奇怪的用工荒，企业找不到足够的人来工作。

sentences.en: Like, I keep seeing things on Twitter about like, the price of lumber being crazy.
sentences.zh: 比如，我一直在推特上看到一些诸如木材价格疯涨之类的事情。

sentences.en: So like, can you please just tell me what is happening and whether I should be storing money under my mattress?
sentences.zh: 所以，请你告诉我到底发生了什么，以及我是不是该把钱藏在床垫底下？

sentences.en: I can tell you not to store money under your mattress.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你不要把钱藏在床垫底下。

sentences.en: That part's easy.
sentences.zh: 那部分很简单。

sentences.en: Okay, whew, that's a relief.
sentences.zh: 好吧，呼，那就放心了。

sentences.en: No, so I will try to answer your questions as best I can, but I'm going to offer a warning
sentences.zh: 不，所以我会尽我所能回答你的问题，但我要在最前面

sentences.en: right up front here, which is that I have no idea what is happening in the economy right now.
sentences.zh: 提出一个警告，那就是我根本不知道现在经济中正在发生什么。

sentences.en: But Ben, if you have no idea, how are any of the rest of us supposed to have an idea?
sentences.zh: 但是本，如果你都不知道，我们其他人怎么可能知道呢？

sentences.en: It is legitimately a really weird moment in the economy.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个非常奇怪的经济时刻。

sentences.en: And there is part of me that wants to say, check back here in six months.
sentences.zh: 我内心有一部分想说，六个月后再来看看。

sentences.en: And I will tell you what has happened in the economy over this period.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉你这段时间经济发生了什么。

sentences.en: But we don't have the luxury of doing that, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们没有奢侈到可以那样做，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we're in the process of making economic policy and making economic decisions.
sentences.zh: 因为我们正处于制定经济政策和做出经济决策的过程中。

sentences.en: And so we sort of have to react to the evidence as we see it in front of us.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须对眼前看到的证据做出反应。

sentences.en: And I'll do my best to help guide you through that.
sentences.zh: 我会尽力引导你度过难关。

sentences.en: But it is a tricky moment where there's a lot of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个充满不确定性的棘手时刻。

sentences.en: Oh, man, this is really, really worrying me.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这真的让我非常非常担心。

sentences.en: This is like when your therapist says, like, I can't do that for you.
sentences.zh: 这就像你的治疗师说，比如，我无法为你做那个。

sentences.en: You have to do that.
sentences.zh: 你必须自己做。

sentences.en: So when did your confusion about what's going on in the economy start?
sentences.zh: 那么，你对经济现状的困惑是从什么时候开始的？

sentences.en: Like, is there a story of the moment where you just realized that, like, you didn't understand things anymore?
sentences.zh: 比如，有没有这样一个瞬间，让你突然意识到，你不再理解这些事情了？

sentences.en: I can tell you exactly when it started, which is Friday, May 7th at 830 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我可以精确地告诉你它是从什么时候开始的，也就是5月7日星期五早上8点30分。

sentences.en: What happened then?
sentences.zh: 那时发生了什么？

sentences.en: What happened was we got the monthly jobs report.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是我们收到了月度就业报告。

sentences.en: So let me step back and give a little bit of context here.
sentences.zh: 所以让我退一步，提供一点背景信息。

sentences.en: We've just come through this year where we all know, right?
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚经历了一年，我们都知道，对吧？

sentences.en: We shut down the economy.
sentences.zh: 我们关闭了经济。

sentences.en: We sort of gradually began to open it back up haltingly over the last year.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，我们以犹豫不决的方式逐渐开始重新开放。

sentences.en: And by the time we got to this spring, it really seemed like we were finally on a glide path back to health.
sentences.zh: 到了今年春天，看起来我们似乎终于走上了恢复健康的滑翔道。

sentences.en: More than 900,000 jobs added to the economy last month.
sentences.zh: 上个月经济新增了超过90万个就业岗位。

sentences.en: That's the largest gain since August and well above what analysts were expecting.
sentences.zh: 这是自8月以来最大幅度的增长，远高于分析师的预期。

sentences.en: We saw some really strong job growth in March.
sentences.zh: 我们在3月份看到了非常强劲的就业增长。

sentences.en: And more and more people getting vaccinated every day.
sentences.zh: 每天都有越来越多的人接种疫苗。

sentences.en: We'd seen vaccines rolling out.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到疫苗在推广。

sentences.en: Finally today, more Americans are vaccinated and getting their shots faster than ever before.
sentences.zh: 终于在今天，更多的美国人接种了疫苗，而且接种速度比以往任何时候都快。

sentences.en: The rollout of the coronavirus vaccine is now fueling hopes that 2021 will see travel take off again.
sentences.zh: 冠状病毒疫苗的推广现在正助长人们的希望，即2021年旅游业将再次腾飞。

sentences.en: We'd seen planes filling up again.
sentences.zh: 我们看到飞机又开始满员了。

sentences.en: We sort of knew that the economy was starting to reopen in a real way.
sentences.zh: 我们多少知道经济开始以一种真正的方式重新开放。

sentences.en: That is some good news.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好消息。

sentences.en: A sign the recovery could be taking hold.
sentences.zh: 复苏可能正在站稳脚跟的迹象。

sentences.en: And we thought that April was really going to be the proof of that.
sentences.zh: 我们以为4月将真正成为这一点的证明。

sentences.en: According to Dow Jones, economists are looking for a gain of about a million jobs in April.
sentences.zh: 据道琼斯报道，经济学家原本预计4月份就业岗位将增加约100万个。

sentences.en: And that's what we all woke up on Friday morning expecting to see.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在周五早晨醒来时期待看到的。

sentences.en: This is like Christmas morning for econ reporters.
sentences.zh: 这就像是经济记者的圣诞节早晨。

sentences.en: Christmas morning, but 12 times a year, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 圣诞节早晨，但一年有12次，凯文。

sentences.en: 12 times a year.
sentences.zh: 一年12次。

sentences.en: Sounds incredibly exciting.
sentences.zh: 听起来令人难以置信地兴奋。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, look, we're all still working from home right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，看，我们现在都还在家办公。

sentences.en: So like I'm in my apartment and my colleagues are all in their apartments and houses.
sentences.zh: 所以就像我在我的公寓里，我的同事们也都在他们的公寓和房子里。

sentences.en: And we're all looking for this big number.
sentences.zh: 我们都在寻找这个巨大的数字。

sentences.en: And the number comes out and it says 266,000 jobs.
sentences.zh: 结果数字出来了，显示是266,000个工作岗位。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这些。

sentences.en: A quarter of what we expected.
sentences.zh: 只有我们预期值的四分之一。

sentences.en: And how shocking is that?
sentences.zh: 这有多令人震惊？

sentences.en: I mean, what's the magnitude of the gap there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那里的差距有多大？

sentences.en: I mean, I think it was pretty shocking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这相当令人震惊。

sentences.en: Nobody's forecast was that low.
sentences.zh: 没有人的预测会这么低。

sentences.en: And so what that told us right off the bat was that this recovery, however it goes, is not going to go the way we all thought at 829 in that morning.
sentences.zh: 所以这直接告诉我们，这次复苏无论如何发展，都不会像我们那天早上8点29分所想的那样进行。

sentences.en: So, Ben, with the caveat that, you know, you are not an all-seeing oracle and maybe don't understand everything that's going on in the economy right now,
sentences.zh: 所以，本，鉴于（你知道的）你不是一个无所不知的先知，可能并不了解现在经济中发生的一切，

sentences.en: but that we can try to piece together some evidence.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以尝试拼凑一些证据。

sentences.en: How do you make sense of these numbers?
sentences.zh: 你如何理解这些数字？

sentences.en: So there are really three theories.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上有三种理论。

sentences.en: The first is in some ways maybe the most obvious, which is that maybe job growth was weaker than we expected in April because the recovery itself is weaker.
sentences.zh: 第一种在某些方面也许是最明显的，那就是4月份的就业增长可能比我们预期的要弱，因为复苏本身比较弱。

sentences.en: Think about the economy right now as a car.
sentences.zh: 把现在的经济想象成一辆汽车。

sentences.en: We're trying to get back up to highway speeds.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图恢复到高速公路的速度。

sentences.en: But maybe we're just kind of still on the access road here, right?
sentences.zh: 但也许我们还只是在匝道上，对吧？

sentences.en: We're not ready to get on the highway.
sentences.zh: 我们还没准备好上高速公路。

sentences.en: We're not ready to start bombing down it at 70 miles an hour because we're still in a pandemic right now.
sentences.zh: 我们还没准备好以每小时70英里的速度在上面狂飙，因为我们现在仍然处于大流行中。

sentences.en: We still can't do all of the things that we're used to being able to do.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然无法做所有我们习惯能够做的事情。

sentences.en: The problem with that theory is that there's a lot of other evidence that we're actually getting back to normal relatively quickly here.
sentences.zh: 那个理论的问题在于，还有很多其他证据表明我们实际上在这里相对较快地恢复正常。

sentences.en: You know, people are getting on airplanes again in large numbers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们又开始大量坐飞机了。

sentences.en: People are going out to eat again, not at the numbers maybe that they were before the pandemic, but certainly growing very quickly.
sentences.zh: 人们又开始出去吃饭了，也许数量没有大流行之前那么多，但肯定在非常迅速地增长。

sentences.en: And, of course, we saw pretty strong numbers in March.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在3月份看到了相当强劲的数字。

sentences.en: So it's a little strange that we would kind of take this step backwards in April.
sentences.zh: 所以在4月份出现这种倒退有点奇怪。

sentences.en: It sort of seems strange that we would lose momentum at a moment when all of the other indications are that actually we should be gaining momentum.
sentences.zh: 在一个所有其他迹象都表明我们实际上应该获得动力的时刻失去动力，似乎有点奇怪。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So that's the first theory.
sentences.zh: 所以那是第一种理论。

sentences.en: What's the second theory?
sentences.zh: 第二种理论是什么？

sentences.en: And if possible, could you return to the metaphor of the car because that was really helping me?
sentences.zh: 如果可能的话，你能回到汽车的比喻吗，因为那真的对我有帮助？

sentences.en: Let's torture this metaphor for as long as we can here.
sentences.zh: 让我们尽可能长时间地折磨这个比喻吧。

sentences.en: So if the first theory is we're stuck on the access road, the second theory is actually we are getting up to speed.
sentences.zh: 所以如果第一种理论是我们被困在匝道上，第二种理论实际上是我们正在加速。

sentences.en: The economy is recovering really quickly.
sentences.zh: 经济恢复得非常快。

sentences.en: But we're in this – we're in a merge, a highway merge moment, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们正处于这个——我们处于一个汇入，一个高速公路汇入的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: And anybody who's merged onto a highway at a busy time of day knows that that can be a tricky moment, right?
sentences.zh: 任何在一天中繁忙时刻汇入高速公路的人都知道那可能是一个棘手的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: You're trying to get over.
sentences.zh: 你正试图并线过去。

sentences.en: You're trying to, you know, get up to speed quickly.
sentences.zh: 你正试图，你知道的，迅速提速。

sentences.en: You're trying to merge into traffic.
sentences.zh: 你正试图汇入车流。

sentences.en: It's tough to go from access road speed to highway speed.
sentences.zh: 从匝道速度提升到高速公路速度很难。

sentences.en: And maybe that's what we're basically seeing here, that a ton of businesses are trying to reopen quickly.
sentences.zh: 也许这正是我们在这里看到的情况，大量的企业正试图迅速重新开业。

sentences.en: They're trying to staff up quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图迅速配备人员。

sentences.en: They have a ton of people that they need to hire.
sentences.zh: 他们有大量的人需要招聘。

sentences.en: Anybody who's hired before knows that even in normal times it's tough to hire quickly.
sentences.zh: 任何有过招聘经验的人都知道，即使在正常时期，快速招聘也很艰难。

sentences.en: And so in this theory, the issue is not that the economy isn't ready to reopen.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种理论中，问题不在于经济没有准备好重新开放。

sentences.en: It's not that we're not ready to get back up to speed.
sentences.zh: 不在于我们没有准备好恢复速度。

sentences.en: It's just that it's tricky to get there.
sentences.zh: 只是要到达那里很棘手。

sentences.en: And it's going to be a couple of months of, you know, pretty crazy numbers back and forth as we try to get ourselves back up to something normal.
sentences.zh: 在我们试图让自己恢复正常状态的过程中，将会有几个月（你知道的）来回波动的疯狂数字。

sentences.en: And then that's all going to flow through and we're going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 然后这一切都会顺理成章地过去，我们会好起来的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So that's theory number two, the tricky merger.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第二种理论，棘手的并线。

sentences.en: What's the third theory?
sentences.zh: 第三种理论是什么？

sentences.en: So the third theory is that actually we're already on the highway.
sentences.zh: 所以第三种理论是，实际上我们已经在高速公路上了。

sentences.en: The economy has kind of emerged from most of its pandemic restrictions already, but we are continuing to jam on that accelerator beyond what the engine can handle.
sentences.zh: 经济已经从其大部分大流行限制中恢复过来，但我们继续猛踩油门，超出了发动机所能承受的范围。

sentences.en: That we are going to risk overheating the engine, overheating the economy,
sentences.zh: 我们面临着让发动机过热、让经济过热的风险，

sentences.en: and ultimately end up in worse shape than if we backed off the accelerator and kind of allowed the economy to continue on its own path.
sentences.zh: 并最终导致情况比我们松开油门并允许经济继续按自身轨迹发展还要糟糕。

sentences.en: So here's what that means in the real world.
sentences.zh: 这就是它在现实世界中的含义。

sentences.en: If we pump too much money into the economy all at once, then it risks basically overwhelming the system.
sentences.zh: 如果我们一次性向经济注入太多资金，那么它基本上就有压垮系统的风险。

sentences.en: When the economy is weak, when people don't have jobs and they don't have money to spend, then the standard economic approach is to give them money.
sentences.zh: 当经济疲软时，当人们没有工作也没有钱花时，标准的经济方法就是给他们钱。

sentences.en: You've got stores that have stuff on their shelves that they want to sell, but they can't sell it right now because people don't have money to spend.
sentences.zh: 你有一些货架上有东西想要出售的商店，但他们现在卖不出去，因为人们没有钱花。

sentences.en: And so we give them money and they spend it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们给他们钱，他们把钱花了。

sentences.en: They go and they buy and we spur economic activity.
sentences.zh: 他们去购买，我们刺激经济活动。

sentences.en: But if we're in a moment when the economy is already good, when factories are already producing as much as they can produce,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们处于经济已经很好的时刻，当工厂已经在生产他们所能生产的最多产品时，

sentences.en: when stores are already selling as much as they produce, then giving people money doesn't actually increase activity.
sentences.zh: 当商店已经在出售他们所能生产的最多东西时，给人们钱实际上并不会增加活动。

sentences.en: It doesn't lead to more spending.
sentences.zh: 它不会带来更多的消费。

sentences.en: It just leads to more competition to buy the stuff that's available, which ultimately just leads to higher prices, which means inflation.
sentences.zh: 它只会导致购买现有物品的竞争加剧，这最终只会导致价格上涨，这意味着通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So what does this jobs report tell us about which scenario we're actually in?
sentences.zh: 那么这份就业报告告诉我们我们实际上处于哪种情境中？

sentences.en: So the trick here is that these can be really difficult to tell apart, especially those last two scenarios.
sentences.zh: 这里的诀窍在于，这些情境很难区分，尤其是最后这两种情境。

sentences.en: And the clearest example of this is the debate over the worker shortage.
sentences.zh: 其中最明显的例子就是关于劳动力短缺的辩论。

sentences.en: Say more about the worker shortage.
sentences.zh: 多讲讲劳动力短缺的事。

sentences.en: So if you talk to almost any business right now, especially businesses like restaurants and hotels and retailers, you hear them complaining that they can't find enough workers,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你现在去跟几乎任何企业交谈，特别是像餐馆、酒店和零售商这样的企业，你会听到他们在抱怨找不到足够的工人，

sentences.en: which on the surface is a pretty surprising thing, right?
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，这挺让人惊讶的对吧？

sentences.en: The unemployment rate is a bit over 6 percent right now.
sentences.zh: 目前的失业率略高于百分之六。

sentences.en: That's down a lot from where it was last spring, but it's still definitely higher than we'd associate with a strong economy.
sentences.zh: 这比去年春天已经大幅下降了，但它绝对仍然高于我们对强劲经济的预期水平。

sentences.en: There's still a lot of people who are out of work.
sentences.zh: 依然有很多人处于失业状态。

sentences.en: And so it's pretty surprising that businesses would be saying, I can't find workers.
sentences.zh: 所以企业会说我找不到工人，这就挺令人惊讶的。

sentences.en: But we see a lot of evidence of this, at least in certain sectors.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到了很多这方面的证据，至少在某些行业是这样。

sentences.en: We see this showing up in different ways in the data.
sentences.zh: 我们看到这些在数据中以不同的方式显现出来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I've seen the, you know, help wanted signs that show up on social media where it's a restaurant saying, you know, basically we can't find enough people to work in the kitchen,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我见过那种社交媒体上发布的招工启事，比如一家餐馆说，基本上我们找不到足够的人来厨房工作，

sentences.en: so we're just going to close down for the time being.
sentences.zh: 所以我们干脆暂时关门歇业。

sentences.en: And so how would someone who believes in your second theory, the sort of tricky merge theory, how would they explain what's happening with worker shortages?
sentences.zh: 那么，相信你第二种理论（也就是那种复杂的融合理论）的人，会如何解释正处于工人短缺中的现状呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So their explanation would be, look, there are a bunch of things that are making it tough for everybody to come back to work right away.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的解释会是，听着，有诸多因素使得每个人都很难立刻重返工作岗位。

sentences.en: So, for example, child care.
sentences.zh: 比如，育儿问题。

sentences.en: I hear all the time from parents of young children that either schools aren't back in person or maybe schools or child care centers are open again, but really erratically, right?
sentences.zh: 我经常听有幼儿的父母说，要么学校没有恢复线下上课，要么学校或托儿所虽然重新开了，但很不规律，对吧？

sentences.en: Everybody's got all these COVID protocols in place.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有一套这样的新冠防疫规程。

sentences.en: And so one kid is sick and all of a sudden everybody's going to be home for the next week or they're at limited hours or only certain days.
sentences.zh: 所以只要有一个孩子生病，突然之间大家接下来的一周都得呆在家，或者实行缩短的工时，又或者只有特定的日子开放。

sentences.en: That makes it really hard to go back to work.
sentences.zh: 这让重返工作岗位变得极其艰难。

sentences.en: Another would be the pandemic itself, the health concerns associated with it.
sentences.zh: 另一个因素就是大流行本身，以及与之相关的健康顾虑。

sentences.en: You know, the data that we're talking about here, this jobs report, the data was collected in early to mid-April,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们在这里讨论的数据，即这份就业报告，其数据是在4月上旬到中旬收集的，

sentences.en: which was a moment at which a lot of Americans were kind of getting their first dose of the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 当时许多美国人正处于接种第一剂疫苗的阶段。

sentences.en: But they weren't yet through unless it was the Johnson & Johnson, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们还没完成全部接种，除非那是强生疫苗，对吧？

sentences.en: They weren't yet through their two doses or their two doses plus two weeks, right?
sentences.zh: 他们还没完成两剂接种，或者说两剂接种加两周的时间，对吧？

sentences.en: So, if you've been careful all year, you've been trying to avoid getting coronavirus and you get the first dose of the vaccine, you may not rush back to work at that point, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你一整年都小心翼翼，一直试图避免感染冠状病毒，而你刚打了第一剂疫苗，你可能不会在那时急着回去上班，对吧？

sentences.en: You may say, I'm going to wait until I've got my two doses in my two weeks and I'm fully vaccinated and I'm all set to go, right?
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，我要等到打完两剂并且过了两周，完全接种好了，一切都准备就绪了再去，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you may still have workers who are not yet totally willing to come back to work.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可能依然会有那些尚未完全愿意重返岗位的工人。

sentences.en: Those are short-term issues, right?
sentences.zh: 这些都是短期问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Sort of by definition.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上可以说是必然的。

sentences.en: People are hopefully going to go and get themselves vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 大家希望都会去接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Schools and child care centers are going to reopen fully.
sentences.zh: 学校和托儿所将全面重新开放。

sentences.en: And so, we just need to sort of get some time for all of this to sort itself through and we'll be kind of back to normal.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们只需要给所有这一切一些时间来自行解决，然后我们就会差不多回到正常状态了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, let's talk now about the people who believe in your third theory in our automotive metaphor here, that we need to ease off on the gas and stop driving like a crazy person.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们现在来聊聊那些相信你的第三种理论的人，用我们汽车的比喻来说，也就是我们需要松一下油门，别再像疯子一样开车了。

sentences.en: What do the people who believe that say is the explanation for this worker shortage?
sentences.zh: 那些相信这一点的人对这次工人短缺有什么解释？

sentences.en: So, the big thing that they point to is unemployment benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们指出最重要的一点就是失业救济金。

sentences.en: During the pandemic, we have expanded unemployment benefits in all sorts of different ways.
sentences.zh: 在大流行期间，我们以各种不同的方式扩大了失业救济金。

sentences.en: We've made them available to people who don't usually get them.
sentences.zh: 我们把它提供给那些通常领不到的人。

sentences.en: We've allowed them to last longer.
sentences.zh: 我们延长了它们的持续时间。

sentences.en: And we've made them more generous.
sentences.zh: 而且我们让它们变得更加丰厚了。

sentences.en: Right now, somebody who's getting unemployment benefits is getting $300 a week from the federal government on top of whatever they get from their normal state benefits.
sentences.zh: 目前，领取失业救济金的人除了能从正常各州福利中获得补贴外，每周还能从联邦政府额外拿到300美元。

sentences.en: And so, the claim that you'll hear from many businesses and from some economists is that
sentences.zh: 因此，你从许多企业和一些经济学家那里听到的说法是

sentences.en: we can't get workers right now because unemployment benefits are disincentivizing them from working.
sentences.zh: 我们现在招不到工人，因为失业救济金消除了他们工作的积极性。

sentences.en: That it's more profitable for them to stay home and collect unemployment benefits than it would be for them to take a job.
sentences.zh: 比起去工作，呆在家里领失业救济金对他们来说更有利可图。

sentences.en: Yeah, look, there are sort of harder and softer versions of this argument, right?
sentences.zh: 对，你看，这种论点有比较强硬和比较温和的版本，对吧？

sentences.en: The sort of hard version is it is literally more profitable for some people to stay home.
sentences.zh: 那种强硬的版本是，对某些人来说呆在家里字面意思上就更有利可图。

sentences.en: They are sitting on the couch playing video games and getting unemployment benefits instead of working.
sentences.zh: 他们正坐在沙发上打电子游戏并领着失业救济金，而不是去工作。

sentences.en: The sort of softer version of this is, look, it may not be that a lot of people are just flat out saying they're not going to work.
sentences.zh: 这种说法的温和版本是，你看，或许并不是很多人直接了当地说他们不打算工作了。

sentences.en: But this makes it easier for them to be pickier about jobs, to hold out for better pay, to wait a little bit longer.
sentences.zh: 但这让他们更容易对工作挑三拣四，坚持等待更高的薪水，再多等上一小会儿。

sentences.en: And so, there are a lot of people who might theoretically be willing to work, but they're not rushing back to work right now because these benefits make it easier.
sentences.zh: 因此，有很多人理论上可能愿意工作，但他们现在并不急着回去上班，因为这些福利让事情变得更容易了。

sentences.en: So, from where you sit, it's kind of hard to tell which of these scenarios is actually playing out in something like the latest jobs report.
sentences.zh: 所以，从你的立场来看，很难分辨这些情景中到底哪一种正在最新的就业报告这类数据中上演。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we're seeing evidence kind of pushing in both directions here, and it's really difficult with just one month of data to tell which of these theories to believe.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我们看到的证据在两个方向上都有推动作用，仅凭一个月的数据真的很难分清应该相信这些理论中的哪一个。

sentences.en: And adding to that is that these different forces are not mutually exclusive.
sentences.zh: 更复杂的是，这些不同的力量并不是互相排斥的。

sentences.en: You know, you could imagine one person who has a kid at home and some child care challenges, who's got concerns about the health of going back to work in the middle of a pandemic,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可以想象这样一个人，家里有个孩子，面临一些育儿方面的挑战，对在疫情期间重返工作岗位的健康问题有所顾虑，

sentences.en: and who is getting these unemployment benefits that make it a little bit easier for them to wait it out until those other things improve.
sentences.zh: 并且正在领取这些失业救济金，这使他们能够更容易地观望，直到那些其他事情有所改善。

sentences.en: And I don't know that you could look at that person and say, well, the reason that they're not working right now is unemployment benefits, or the reason is child care.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你能不能看着这样一个人说，嗯，他们现在不工作的原因是失业救济金，或者原因是为了照顾孩子。

sentences.en: It's all of these things working together.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素都在共同起作用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That makes sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说说得通。

sentences.en: People's lives are complex.
sentences.zh: 人们的生活是复杂的。

sentences.en: These factors might be simultaneously happening in ways that are hard to just see in one jobs report.
sentences.zh: 这些因素可能同时在发生，其方式很难仅仅从一份就业报告中看出来。

sentences.en: But I wonder, is there other data, are there other reports, other indicators that might help point us to which of these scenarios is most true right now?
sentences.zh: 但我想知道，是否还有其他数据、其他报告、其他指标，能够帮助我们指出当前哪种情景最符合真实情况？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, in fact, there was another report that came out less than a week after that big jobs report that we were all looking at for evidence.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我们都在寻找证据的那份重大就业报告发布不到一周后，还有另一份报告出炉了。

sentences.en: And this was the report on inflation.
sentences.zh: 这就是关于通货膨胀的报告。

sentences.en: And it was another huge surprise.
sentences.zh: 而且这是又一个巨大的惊喜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能获取所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你就可以。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Ben, I'm picturing you again at your computer looking for a new report, furiously refreshing the page.
sentences.zh: 所以，本，我脑海中又浮现出你坐在电脑前寻找新报告、疯狂刷新页面的样子。

sentences.en: But this time you're waiting for inflation numbers, not jobs numbers.
sentences.zh: 但这次你等的是通胀数据，而不是就业数据。

sentences.en: So, what were your expectations for these numbers?
sentences.zh: 那么，你对这些数据的预期是什么？

sentences.en: And then what actually happened?
sentences.zh: 然后实际发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so this report was the Consumer Price Index, which we're way into econ nerddom when we start getting excited about the CPI report.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这份报告是消费者物价指数，当我们开始对CPI报告感到兴奋时，说明我们已经深深陷入了经济学书呆子的圈子。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was going to say, Ben, this is a family show.
sentences.zh: 对，我本来想说，本，这是一个适合全家观看的节目。

sentences.en: Please keep it PG-13.
sentences.zh: 请把它保持在PG-13级别（适合13岁以上观看）。

sentences.en: So, this is basically the government's effort to estimate what is happening with the prices that consumers pay.
sentences.zh: 所以，这基本上是政府为了估算消费者支付的价格正在发生什么变化而做出的努力。

sentences.en: So, it's prices on everything from, you know, beef and bread to cars and air travel and everything that we spend.
sentences.zh: 因此，它是从牛肉和面包到汽车、机票以及我们消费的一切东西的价格。

sentences.en: And how much did prices rise in a given month?
sentences.zh: 以及在给定的一个月里价格上涨了多少？

sentences.en: And everyone thought that this report would show that prices rose in April and actually rose a pretty good amount.
sentences.zh: 每个人都以为这份报告会显示4月份物价上涨了，而且实际上确实上涨了相当不错的幅度。

sentences.en: Because, again, we're in this reopening moment.
sentences.zh: 因为，再次说明，我们正处于这个重新开放的时期。

sentences.en: Forecasters thought it would show an increase of about two-tenths of a percentage point from March to April,
sentences.zh: 预测人士原本认为它会显示从3月到4月上涨大约十分之二个百分点，

sentences.en: which sounds very, very small, but, of course, it's just one month, so it actually would be pretty meaningful.
sentences.zh: 这听起来非常非常小，但当然，这只是一个月的数据，所以它实际上会相当有意义。

sentences.en: But that's not what we saw at all.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到的根本不是那回事。

sentences.en: We saw much faster gains.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了快得多的涨幅。

sentences.en: We saw eight-tenths of a percentage point.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了十分之八个百分点。

sentences.en: Again, sounds small, but four times what economists were expecting to see.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，听起来很小，但这是经济学家预期值的四倍。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And, like, give me an example of how these price increases are actually showing up in the economy.
sentences.zh: 而且，能给我举个例子说明这些价格上涨是如何真正在经济中显现出来的吗？

sentences.en: So, a lot of it is exactly what we would expect.
sentences.zh: 所以，很大一部分完全符合我们的预期。

sentences.en: Airfares were up.
sentences.zh: 机票价格上涨了。

sentences.en: Hotels were up.
sentences.zh: 酒店价格上涨了。

sentences.en: Rental cars were up.
sentences.zh: 租车价格上涨了。

sentences.en: This is all the stuff that we weren't doing and now we're doing it, and so those prices are rising quickly.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们以前不做、现在正在做的事情，所以这些价格正在迅速上涨。

sentences.en: They're rising even faster than we expected, but we're not surprised that they're rising.
sentences.zh: 它们的上涨速度甚至比我们预期的还要快，但它们在上涨这件事并不让我们感到意外。

sentences.en: There are others that might be a little bit less intuitive.
sentences.zh: 还有一些可能没那么直观。

sentences.en: Used car prices were up 10% from March to April.
sentences.zh: 二手车价格从3月到4月上涨了10%。

sentences.en: A 10% increase in used car prices in one month.
sentences.zh: 二手车价格在一个月内上涨了10%。

sentences.en: That's pretty wild.
sentences.zh: 这相当疯狂。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's nuts.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: So, 10% in one month.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个月内上涨10%。

sentences.en: And, like, I haven't bought a car recently, but to put that in real terms, like, people who were shopping for a car earlier this year,
sentences.zh: 而且，就像，我最近没买过车，但为了把它转化为实际的价值，比如，今年早些时候买车的人，

sentences.en: maybe their budget was, you know, $10,000, but if they waited a month, if they bought it in April, that $10,000 car they wanted is now $11,000.
sentences.zh: 也许他们的预算是，你知道的，10,000美元，但如果他们等了一个月，如果他们在4月份买，他们想要的那个10,000美元的车现在变成11,000美元了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a pretty big penalty for waiting a month.
sentences.zh: 为了等一个月要付出相当大的代价。

sentences.en: And why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Like, why did prices of used cars go up so much so quickly?
sentences.zh: 为什么二手车价格会如此大幅度、如此迅速地上涨？

sentences.en: So, I think this is actually a great example of sort of how the economy is complicated right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这实际上是一个很好的例子，说明了当前经济是如何复杂的。

sentences.en: So, one of the reasons for this is that a lot of the used cars that you buy are actually former rental cars.
sentences.zh: 所以，原因之一是，你买的许多二手车实际上都是以前的租赁车。

sentences.en: Rental car companies buy a ton of cars.
sentences.zh: 租车公司购买大量的汽车。

sentences.en: They use them for, you know, a year, and then they sell them off to used car lots.
sentences.zh: 他们使用它们，你知道的，一年，然后把它们卖给二手车行。

sentences.en: Well, rental car companies, a year ago, when everything shut down, they were not buying cars.
sentences.zh: 好吧，租车公司在一年前，当一切都关闭的时候，他们没有买车。

sentences.en: In fact, they were selling off a lot of cars.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们正在抛售大量的汽车。

sentences.en: And so, now, fast forward a year later, they don't have any cars to sell.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，快进到一年后，他们没有任何车可以卖了。

sentences.en: And so, we've got fewer rental cars turning into used cars.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们发现转化为二手车的租赁车辆变少了。

sentences.en: That's happening at the exact same moment that a lot of people are going back to work, but maybe they don't want to get on the subway yet or the bus quite yet.
sentences.zh: 这正发生在大量人员重返工作岗位、但可能还不想搭乘地铁或公交车的同一时刻。

sentences.en: So, they're buying up a used car.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在抢购二手车。

sentences.en: And so, we've got demand rising at a moment when supply is, for some sort of weird technical reasons, a little bit limited.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在供应由于某种奇怪的技术原因而略显紧缺的时刻，迎来了需求的增长。

sentences.en: And so, all of a sudden, prices spike.
sentences.zh: 于是，突然之间，价格飙升。

sentences.en: So, I get the used car case and why the fact that rental car companies weren't buying cars last year
sentences.zh: 所以我理解二手车的情况，以及为什么租车公司去年没有买车

sentences.en: means that there are fewer used cars on the market today, which makes the prices go higher.
sentences.zh: 意味着今天市场上二手车变少了，从而导致价格上涨。

sentences.en: But this isn't just happening with cars, right?
sentences.zh: 但这不仅发生在汽车上，对吧？

sentences.en: It's happening with the price of lumber, with the price of, you know, chicken parts.
sentences.zh: 它发生在木材价格上，你知道的，还有鸡肉分割肉的价格上。

sentences.en: Like, the taco place that I get takeout from all the time just raised its menu prices.
sentences.zh: 就像我经常去买外卖的那家墨西哥卷饼店刚刚提高了菜单价格一样。

sentences.en: So, are all of these just kind of individual stories with their own nuances and particulars?
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些都只是一些各有其细微差别和特性的独立故事吗？

sentences.en: Or is this all part of one bigger story?
sentences.zh: 还是这都是一个宏大故事的一部分？

sentences.en: So, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And this is, again, where we run into this problem of it being hard to tell apart these different theories of what's happening.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们再次遇到这个问题的地方，即很难分辨关于正在发生的事情的这些不同理论。

sentences.en: So, the conventional theory right now, and this is the one that is held to by the Fed and by most economists that I talk to,
sentences.zh: 所以，目前的传统理论（这也是美联储和我交谈过的大多数经济学家所持有的理论），

sentences.en: is that pretty much all of this are these weird short-term things that are happening in the economy.
sentences.zh: 是几乎所有这些都是经济中发生的奇怪的短期现象。

sentences.en: The word that the Fed keeps using is transitory.
sentences.zh: 美联储一直使用的词是“暂时的”。

sentences.en: And actually, if you look at a lot of the categories that are not heavily affected by these sorts of issues, you don't really see rapid inflation.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你看看许多未受此类问题严重影响的类别，你并不会真正看到快速的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Rents, for example, have really been quite tame.
sentences.zh: 例如，租金一直相当温和。

sentences.en: We haven't seen a ton of inflation in healthcare, in some of these other categories that are sort of outside of our immediate sort of pandemic weirdness.
sentences.zh: 我们在医疗保健以及其他一些超出了我们直接的大流行怪异现象的类别中，并没有看到大量的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And so, most economists look at that and they say, we've got to wait for kind of all this to pass by,
sentences.zh: 因此，大多数经济学家看到这一点时，他们会说，我们必须等待这一切过去，

sentences.en: and then inflation is going to settle back down and it's not going to be that big a deal.
sentences.zh: 然后通货膨胀就会回落，而且不会是什么大不了的事。

sentences.en: But the fear with inflation is that it can become a self-fulfilling prophecy.
sentences.zh: 但对通胀的担忧在于，它可能会变成一种自我实现的预言。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: So, if prices go up a little bit one week or one month, you probably just kind of shrug your shoulders.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果价格在一个星期或一个月内稍微上涨了一点，你可能只会耸耸肩。

sentences.en: This is life.
sentences.zh: 这就是生活。

sentences.en: But there's a certain point at which, if every time you go to the grocery store, prices are higher.
sentences.zh: 但在某个特定的点上，如果你每次去杂货店，价格都更高。

sentences.en: If every time you go out and spend money, prices are higher.
sentences.zh: 如果你每次出门花钱，价格都更高。

sentences.en: You're going to go to your boss and you're going to say, come on, you've got to give me more money here because you've seen what's going on with prices.
sentences.zh: 你就会去找你的老板，然后你会说，得了吧，你得给我更多的钱，因为你已经看到了价格发生的变化。

sentences.en: I can't afford to buy anything anymore.
sentences.zh: 我已经买不起任何东西了。

sentences.en: And then the boss has got to go and raise prices so that he can pay for your increased salary.
sentences.zh: 然后老板不得不提高价格，以便支付你增加的工资。

sentences.en: And we get this cycle.
sentences.zh: 我们就陷入了这个循环。

sentences.en: Or think about it with the products that go into whatever it is you're making.
sentences.zh: 或者想想你正在制造的任何产品所涉及的原材料。

sentences.en: If you're a McDonald's and beef prices are rising and potato prices are rising, now you've got to go and raise prices.
sentences.zh: 如果你经营一家麦当劳，牛肉价格在上涨，土豆价格在上涨，现在你就不得不去涨价。

sentences.en: And this starts to flow its way through the economy to the point that people now expect inflation to be higher.
sentences.zh: 这开始在整个经济体系中传导，以至于人们现在开始预期通货膨胀会更高。

sentences.en: Instead of thinking that they live in a world where prices rise a percent or two percent or three percent a year,
sentences.zh: 他们不再认为自己生活在一个物价每年上涨百分之一、百分之二或百分之三的世界里，

sentences.en: now they start expecting prices to rise four and five and six percent a year.
sentences.zh: 现在他们开始预期物价每年上涨百分之四、百分之五和百分之六。

sentences.en: And they demand the raises and prices rise in accordance with that expectation.
sentences.zh: 他们要求加薪，物价也随之按照这种预期上涨。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, we live in a world where that's just the reality, where prices rise five percent a year.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我们生活在一个这就是现实的世界里，物价每年上涨百分之五。

sentences.en: And so if people do start acting as if they think inflation is coming,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人们真的开始表现得好像他们认为通货膨胀即将到来一样，

sentences.en: what specifically would you be worried about happening?
sentences.zh: 具体来说，你会担心发生什么？

sentences.en: So I think this is where there are two concerns.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这里有两个担忧。

sentences.en: One is that that really does become a self-fulfilling prophecy.
sentences.zh: 一个是这真的会变成一种自我实现的预言。

sentences.en: And inflation starts rising.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀开始上升。

sentences.en: It becomes faster than we've been comfortable with in recent years.
sentences.zh: 它的增速将超过我们近年来所能适应的水平。

sentences.en: And that's – look, that's bad news for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 看，这对很多人来说都不是好消息。

sentences.en: That's bad news for anybody who's sitting on savings in a savings account where the value of that gets slower.
sentences.zh: 对于任何把钱存在储蓄账户里而其价值在不断缩水的人来说，这不是好消息。

sentences.en: It's bad news for anybody on a fixed income who is not seeing their income rise along with inflation
sentences.zh: 对于任何固定收入者来说，这不是好消息，他们的收入并没有随着通货膨胀而增加，

sentences.en: and therefore is taking – is seeing their income and its actual buying power decline.
sentences.zh: 因此他们的收入及其实际购买力正在下降。

sentences.en: It's bad news for businesses that are trying to navigate a world in which their input prices are rising really rapidly.
sentences.zh: 对于那些正试图应付投入品价格飞涨的世界的企业来说，这不是好消息。

sentences.en: So that's one concern.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个担忧。

sentences.en: The other concern is that the Federal Reserve looks at that possibility, becomes concerned about it, and says, we better get control of this before it gets out of control.
sentences.zh: 另一个担忧是，美联储看到了这种可能性，对此感到担忧，并表示，我们最好在它失控之前控制住它。

sentences.en: And so they raise interest rates to try to slow down the economy, and we end up needing to weaken the economy intentionally in order to prevent that run-up in prices.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们提高利率以试图放缓经济，我们最终需要刻意削弱经济，以防止物价飙升。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: That the government, the Federal Reserve, could essentially start a recession on purpose in order to deal with the threat of inflation.
sentences.zh: 政府、美联储为了应对通货膨胀的威胁，实际上可以故意引发一场经济衰退。

sentences.en: Look, this is what happened in the 1970s and early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 看，这就是上世纪70年代和80年代初发生的事情。

sentences.en: We saw in the 60s and 70s, for a variety of reasons, inflation really pick up.
sentences.zh: 我们在60年代和70年代看到，由于各种原因，通货膨胀确实大幅上升。

sentences.en: And the only way that we got it under control was that the Fed stepped in and hiked interest rates so high that it crushed the housing market, it eventually crushed the job market,
sentences.zh: 我们控制住它的唯一方法就是美联储介入并将利率提高到如此之高，以至于它摧毁了房地产市场，最终摧毁了就业市场，

sentences.en: and created a really punishing, brutal recession.
sentences.zh: 并造成了一场惩罚性的、残酷的经济衰退。

sentences.en: They succeeded.
sentences.zh: 他们成功了。

sentences.en: They got control of inflation, but at a tremendous cost to a huge number of Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们控制住了通货膨胀，但代价对广大美国人民来说是巨大的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the next time we get jobs numbers or inflation numbers in the coming months,
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几个月里，当我们拿到就业数据或通货膨胀数据时，

sentences.en: will this debate be settled?
sentences.zh: 这场争论会平息吗？

sentences.en: Will we know if this was, in fact, a transitory thing, or if this was some signal of a more permanent problem?
sentences.zh: 我们会知道这实际上是一个暂时的现象，还是某种更持久的问题的信号？

sentences.en: We will eventually.
sentences.zh: 我们最终会知道的。

sentences.en: We won't necessarily right away.
sentences.zh: 不一定马上就能知道。

sentences.en: You know, look, on a certain level, if we continue to see these trends play out, right, that's going to add to these concerns.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从某种程度上讲，如果我们继续看到这些趋势上演，对吧，这会加剧这些担忧。

sentences.en: If it starts to reverse, then that's going to ease some of those concerns.
sentences.zh: 如果它开始逆转，那么这些担忧就会缓解。

sentences.en: But this highway merge is not expected to take just one month or just two months.
sentences.zh: 但这条高速公路的合并预计不会只花一个月或两个月时间。

sentences.en: It's expected to take a little bit of time as we get vaccines out there, as we reopen schools, as we work through all of these constraints in the economy right now.
sentences.zh: 随着我们分发疫苗、重新开放学校、解决目前经济中的所有这些制约因素，这需要一段时间。

sentences.en: And the fact that these problems continued for another month doesn't tell us that those problems are going to persist for an extended period of time.
sentences.zh: 这些问题再持续一个月，并不意味着这些问题会长期持续下去。

sentences.en: It just tells us that we're not past that period yet.
sentences.zh: 它只是告诉我们，我们还没有度过那个时期。

sentences.en: And so on some level, it's really probably not going to be until the fall that we have a clear signal of whether this was a transitory period
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种程度上说，可能要到秋天，我们才能对这究竟是一个过渡时期，

sentences.en: or something more concerning and more lasting.
sentences.zh: 还是一个更令人担忧、更持久的问题有一个清晰的信号。

sentences.en: I mean, this seems to be happening very quickly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这似乎发生得非常快。

sentences.en: Like, if you are the Federal Reserve or the government, you're trying to figure out, you know, do we extend unemployment benefits?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你是美联储或政府，你在设法弄清楚，你知道，我们要延长失业救济金吗？

sentences.en: Do we raise interest rates?
sentences.zh: 我们要提高利率吗？

sentences.en: Whatever you might do as a government to sort of control the possibility of inflation, like, that seems like a decision they have to make pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 无论政府可能采取什么措施来控制通胀的可能性，这似乎都是他们必须相当快做出决定的事情。

sentences.en: They might not actually want to wait until the fall.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上可能不想等到秋天。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is all playing out at a moment when a lot of these decisions are being made.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一切都在许多此类决策正在做出的时刻展开。

sentences.en: Now, the Federal Reserve has made quite clear that they are not going to change their policy
sentences.zh: 现在，美联储已经非常明确地表示，他们不会因为几个月的数据而改变政策，

sentences.en: because of a couple months of data, and I think there's very little reason to doubt them at this point.
sentences.zh: 我认为目前几乎没有理由怀疑他们。

sentences.en: On the political side, this is a very real discussion happening right now.
sentences.zh: 在政治方面，这正是当前正在进行的一场非常真实的讨论。

sentences.en: We have several states that have actually said, forget it, we are cutting off these extra unemployment benefits because we think it's holding back the economy.
sentences.zh: 我们有几个州实际上已经表示，算了吧，我们要切断这些额外的失业救济金，因为我们认为它阻碍了经济发展。

sentences.en: And then you have other states, mostly run by Democrats, that are saying, no, we're going to keep on this path.
sentences.zh: 然后还有其他州，大多由民主党人掌控，他们说，不，我们要继续走这条路。

sentences.en: And look, for economists, that has an advantage to it, which is that as states go in different directions, we're going to kind of get to test these theories.
sentences.zh: 而且你看，对于经济学家来说，这有一个好处，那就是随着各州朝着不同的方向发展，我们将有机会检验这些理论。

sentences.en: If Montana cuts off unemployment benefits and we see a big surge in people going to work in Montana, that gives us a pretty good indication of what was going on there.
sentences.zh: 如果蒙大拿州切断了失业救济金，并且我们看到蒙大拿州去工作的人数激增，这让我们对那里发生的事情有了相当好的了解。

sentences.en: If, instead, people don't have money to spend there anymore and we see a fallback in activity, that gives us a sense that, no, the real problem here was the economy
sentences.zh: 相反，如果人们在那里再也没有钱花，并且我们看到经济活动回落，这就让我们有一种感觉，不，这里真正的的问题是经济

sentences.en: was not ready for that support to get pulled out from under it.
sentences.zh: 还没有准备好让这种支持从它脚下被抽走。

sentences.en: So we're going to get some answers to this, but somebody's right and somebody's wrong, and there's going to be costs for the people in the states that get it wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会得到一些答案，但总有人对，总有人错，而那些搞错方向的州的人民将付出代价。

sentences.en: Ben, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 本，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 停火的可能性依然渺茫。

sentences.zh: 尽管包括美国在内的多国努力通过外交手段结束暴力，但以色列和哈马斯双方周一还是发动了新一轮袭击。

sentences.en: And just as in World War II, America was the arsenal of democracy in the battle against the COVID-19 pandemic,
sentences.zh: 正如在第二次世界大战中，美国是打击新冠疫情战役中的民主兵工厂一样，

sentences.en: our nation is going to be the arsenal of vaccines for the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家也将成为世界其他地区的疫苗兵工厂。

sentences.en: President Biden has announced a plan to deliver 20 million doses of the three COVID-19 vaccines already authorized for use in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统已经宣布了一项计划，将向受疫情挣扎的外国提供2000万剂已获准在美国使用的三种新冠疫苗。

sentences.en: to foreign countries struggling with the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 向受疫情困扰的外国提供。

sentences.en: In a speech, Biden said that the United States would never be truly protected from the virus until the rest of the world was also vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 拜登在一次演讲中表示，在世界其他地方也接种疫苗之前，美国永远不会真正免受病毒的侵害。

sentences.en: No oceans wide enough, no walls high enough to keep us safe.
sentences.zh: 没有足够宽的海洋，没有足够高的墙能保证我们的安全。

sentences.en: The 20 million vaccine doses from Pfizer, Moderna, and Johnson & Johnson will be in addition to the 60 million doses that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 来自辉瑞、莫德纳和强生的2000万剂疫苗将是对美国承诺从海外运送的60万剂（注：原文60 million译为6000万剂）阿斯利康疫苗的补充，这些阿斯利康疫苗尚未获准在美国使用。

sentences.en: has pledged to send overseas from AstraZeneca, which are not yet authorized for use in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国尚未获准使用阿斯利康疫苗，美国承诺向海外运送6000万剂阿斯利康疫苗，这2000万剂疫苗将是这些之外的补充。

sentences.zh: 这是正确的事。

sentences.en: It's the smart thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这是明智的事。

sentences.zh: 这是强有力的事。
